fixes.explanation: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, goes down and finds the potter "…working at the wheel." (Jeremiah 18:3) The LORD had told him to go there, and that He would give His message at the potter's house (Jeremiah 18:2). I think this is a scene where you simply watch and learn. Sometimes the best classroom is somebody else's workshop.

Setting it aside to dry isn't in the verse. The potter shapes it again, and “…he formed it into another vessel, as it seemed best for him to do.” (Jeremiah 18:4) The flawed vessel becomes another vessel in his hands.

A second nation doesn't show up in this verse. The LORD says, “…then I will relent of the good I had intended for it.” (Jeremiah 18:10) Passing it to another isn't something the verse says. I can see why you'd guess it, though.
Praise isn't the word in the verse. The LORD says, “Yet My people have forgotten Me.” (Jeremiah 18:15) The verse goes on to say they burn incense to worthless idols.

That's what the LORD says: they're “…leaving the ancient roads to walk on rutted bypaths instead of on the highway.” (Jeremiah 18:15) Rutted bypaths sound bumpy to me. Think of rolling dough across a counter covered in crumbs. Nothing comes out smooth.

Egypt and the wilderness don't show up in this verse. The LORD says they're “…leaving the ancient roads to walk on rutted bypaths instead of on the highway.” (Jeremiah 18:15) The picture is walking on bypaths instead of on the highway. It's an easy mix-up with other Bible journeys, but not this one.

Yes. The LORD says the land will be a desolation, and “all who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.” (Jeremiah 18:16) Everybody passing by gets the same reaction. That's a lot of head shaking, if you ask me.

That's their plan. Some people say, “Come, let us denounce him and pay no heed to any of his words.” (Jeremiah 18:18) The "him" is Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet. It's like muting a group chat so you never have to read what's in it.

No king appears in this verse. Some people speak about Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, and say, “Come, let us denounce him and pay no heed to any of his words.” (Jeremiah 18:18) Their plan is to denounce him and pay no heed to his words. Bringing them to the king isn't part of it.

Nobody grabs a scroll here. Some people speak about Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, and say, “Come, let us denounce him and pay no heed to any of his words.” (Jeremiah 18:18) Writing isn't part of what they say. Their plan is to denounce him and pay no heed to his words.
